brief: Hungary's payments/banking trade-media layer is small, concentrated and unusually quantitative: Portfolio.hu's Bank desk, the VG group's bonline.hu, and the two fintech specialists (FinTechZone, Fintech.hu) between them convert almost every MNB pénzforgalmi release into charted analysis within days, and add acquirer- and vendor-level figures obtained by interview — qvik volumes from SimplePay, the first-ever decline in physical card-accepting locations, PSP revenue and fraud-loss totals. A second, structurally different tier consists of comparison portals (Bank360, Bankmonitor, Biztosdöntés, Money.hu) that compile bank-by-bank account, card and cash-withdrawal fee data from hirdetmény documents; this pricing data is genuinely unavailable in aggregated form anywhere else and is best treated as a direct source, subject to ToS checks. Consumer-facing volume outlets (Pénzcentrum, Origo, the county-daily network) are low-credibility on their own but give early and geographically granular signals on ATM-network restructuring and cash-access rule changes. Nothing in this cell publishes machine-readable data, so collection must be HU-language text extraction with mandatory reconciliation back to statisztika.mnb.hu; note also that 'POS terminál' is a heavily vendor-spammed query term and that neither napi.hu nor vg.hu produced any article-level hits in this pass.
